results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

Since you'd like to appeal this policy decision, this needs a specialist, so I've passed it on. Your case number is CASE-20261008-181539-9b1dfe. A specialist will review it soon. This case already includes everything from our conversation, so you won't need to repeat yourself.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: Why was my CBD candle disapproved?
turns.reply:
Your product "CBD Infused Lavender Relaxation Candle, 6 oz" (ID: HG-023) was disapproved because it mentions CBD.

Under Google's policy, cannabidiol (CBD) is included on the list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements, and products containing or mentioning CBD are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings. Because this is a policy rule rather than a data error, it cannot be fixed by editing product details. For more details, see [CBD and other unapproved substances](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6165956).

If you believe this decision is incorrect, you can request a review by choosing "I disagree with the issue" in Merchant Center. Keep in mind that you may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, as outlined in [Requesting a review or appealing a decision](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13585221).

If you would like to appeal this decision, please let me know and I can transfer your case to a specialist. Would you like to do that, or move on to the other product issues?

turns.merchant: Could some automatic setting fill in the missing barcodes for me?
turns.reply:
There are no account issues and no disapproved products, but 2 products have a warning for a missing product barcode number (GTIN), which limits their visibility.

No automatic setting can fill in missing barcodes for you. Automatic item updates only cover price, sale price, availability, and condition, as explained in [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284).

Here are the 2 affected products with missing product barcode numbers (GTIN):
- **HG-002 "Linen Napkins, Set of 4, Natural"**: Missing product barcode number (GTIN).
- **HG-007 "Wool Throw Blanket, Charcoal Herringbone"**: Missing product barcode number (GTIN).

To fix this manually:
- If these items have barcode numbers from the manufacturer or supplier, add the exact 8, 12, 13, or 14-digit number to your product data. Never make up a number.
- If a product does not have a barcode number (such as a store brand), leave GTIN blank and provide the brand and manufacturer part number (MPN) instead. For details, see [Product barcode number (GTIN)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324461).
- If the product truly has no identifiers at all (no GTIN, MPN, or brand), you can set identifier exists to "no", as outlined in [Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324478).

Would you like help with anything else on this issue, or should we move on?

turns.merchant: Is there any automatic option that could deal with my lamp and shelf pictures?
turns.reply:
No, an automatic option cannot fix these picture issues.

### Account Overview
* **Account issues:** None
* **Disapprovals:** 2 products are disapproved because of missing or placeholder image links.
* **Warnings:** None

### Image Issues
Your settings show that **automatic image improvements** are already turned on. However, as noted in [Automatic image improvements](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9242973), this feature only removes promotional overlays (like text or watermarks) from existing photos. It cannot add a missing image or replace a placeholder image with a real product photo.

To fix these products, you must update the data manually as outlined in [Product image link](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350):

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)

turns.merchant: Why are two of my products not showing?
turns.reply:
You have no account-level issues. 2 products are disapproved because of invalid or placeholder image links, and there are no warnings.

Here are the disapproved products:
- **HG-006 "Ceramic Table Lamp, Matte White"**: No main product image link is set.
- **HG-013 "Walnut Wall Shelf, 24 inch"**: The image link points to a placeholder image (`https://cdn.hearthandhollow.example/img/placeholder.png`) rather than a real product photo.

### How to fix
To resolve this, provide a full web address starting with `http://` or `https://` pointing to a real image of each actual product. Placeholders or generic graphics are not allowed, and images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels without promotional text or overlays. For more details, see [Product image link](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350).

*Note on automatic improvements:* Automatic image improvements only remove promotional overlays from existing photos; they cannot fix missing or placeholder images. You must add a real product image manually ([Automatic image improvements](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9242973)).

Would you like to move on or do you have any questions about fixing these images?

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: What's wrong with my products?
turns.reply:
You have no account-level issues. Currently, 13 products are disapproved, mainly due to price mismatches, invalid image links, long titles, availability mismatches, missing shipping information, and a restricted product policy issue. Additionally, 6 products have warnings (demotions) for missing product barcode numbers (GTINs).

Let's start with the largest disapproval issue, which is **price mismatch** affecting 3 products:

- **HG-004 "Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage"**: Feed price is 32.00 USD, but your website shows 36.00 USD.
- **HG-015 "Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper"**: Feed price is 58.00 USD, but your website shows 64.00 USD.
- **HG-021 "Stainless Steel Kettle, 1.7 L"**: Feed price is 48.00 USD, but your website shows 44.00 USD.

**How to fix:**
To fix this manually, update the price in your product data so it matches the price on your product page exactly, then upload the updated data ([Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029)). 

Since automatic price updates are currently turned off in your account settings, I also recommend turning on automatic item updates for price under **Products** > **Automations** in Merchant Center. This allows Google to automatically update prices from your website and prevent future mismatches ([Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284)).

Would you like to move on to the next issue?

turns.reply:
Your account has no account-level issues. Currently, 1 product is disapproved due to a price mismatch, and there are no warnings.

**Disapproved product:**
- **Title:** Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage (ID: `HG-004`)
- **Issue:** The price in your product data is 32.00 USD, but your website product page shows 36.00 USD.

**How to fix it:**
To fix this issue, update the price in your product data to match the price on your website (36.00 USD) and re-upload your data. Once updated, Google will recheck the page, which usually takes a few hours to days, and approve the product once the prices match. For more information, see [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029).

**Preventing future mismatches:**
To help avoid price mismatches, we recommend turning on automatic price updates in Merchant Center under **Products > Automations**. This allows Google to automatically update the price in your product data using the price found on your website. Learn more in [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284).

Would you like to review anything else?

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)

turns.reply:
No, editing the product description will not get it approved. CBD is included on Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements, so products containing CBD are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings ([CBD and other unapproved substances](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6165956)). Keep in mind that you may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period applies.

turns.merchant: What's wrong with my products?
turns.reply:
Here is a summary of your account and product issues:

- **Account issues:** None
- **Disapproved products:** 13 products are disapproved due to price mismatches (3), invalid image links (3), titles being too long (2), availability mismatches (2), missing shipping information (2), and restricted product policy (1).
- **Warnings:** 6 products are demoted due to a missing product barcode number (GTIN).

### Disapproval Issue 1: Price Mismatch
3 products have a price in your product data that does not match the price on your website. When prices do not match, Google disapproves the products ([Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029)).

**Affected products:**
- **HG-004 "Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage"**: Product feed price is $32.00 USD, but the website shows $36.00 USD.
- **HG-015 "Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper"**: Product feed price is $58.00 USD, but the website shows $64.00 USD.
- **HG-021 "Stainless Steel Kettle, 1.7 L"**: Product feed price is $48.00 USD, but the website shows $44.00 USD.

**How to fix:**
Update the price in your product data to match your website exactly and upload the updated feed. Google will recheck the pages and reapprove the items once they match. 

To help prevent this in the future, you can also turn on **automatic price updates** under **Products > Automations** in Merchant Center ([Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284)).

Would you like to move on to the next issue?

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.reply:
Here is an overview of your account status:

- **Account issues:** None.
- **Disapprovals:** 13 products are disapproved and cannot show in Shopping ads or free listings. The main reasons are price mismatches, invalid or missing images, titles that exceed the character limit, availability mismatches, missing shipping details, and a restricted product policy issue.
- **Warnings:** 6 products are missing a product barcode number (GTIN), which limits their visibility.

---

### Price Mismatches (3 products disapproved)
Google found that the price in your product data does not match the price on your website.

**Affected products:**
- **HG-004** "Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage": Feed price is 32.00 USD, but the product page shows 36.00 USD.
- **HG-015** "Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper": Feed price is 58.00 USD, but the product page shows 64.00 USD.

Update the price in your product data so it matches your product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. Learn more in [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029).

**Recommendation:**
Your automatic price updates setting is currently turned off. To help avoid price mismatches in the future, you can turn on automatic item updates. Learn more in [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284).

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability

turns.merchant: What's wrong with my products?
turns.reply:
You currently have no account-level issues and no warnings. However, 4 products are disapproved: 2 due to price mismatches and 2 due to missing images.

### Price Mismatch (2 products)
Your product feed price must match the price shown on your website and at checkout ([Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029)). The following products are affected:
- **Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage** (ID: `HG-004`): Feed price is 32.00 USD, but the product page shows 36.00 USD.
- **Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper** (ID: `HG-015`): Feed price is 58.00 USD, but the product page shows 64.00 USD.

**How to fix:** Update the prices in your product data to match your product pages exactly and re-upload your feed. Once updated, Google will recheck the pages over the next few hours or days ([Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029)).

**Recommendation:** Your automatic price updates setting is currently off. You can turn on automatic item updates under Products > Automations in Merchant Center to automatically update product prices based on your website's structured data ([Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284)).

Would you like to move on to the next issue regarding your product images?

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: What's wrong with my products?
turns.reply:
Your account has no account-level issues. However, 13 products are disapproved due to price mismatches, invalid images, titles being too long, availability mismatches, missing shipping information, and restricted product policy. Additionally, 6 products have warnings for a missing product barcode number (GTIN).

Let's address the price mismatch issue first, which affects 3 products. The price listed in your product feed does not match what appears on your website checkout page:
- **HG-004**: "Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage" — Feed price is 32.00 USD, but website shows 36.00 USD.
- **HG-015**: "Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper" — Feed price is 58.00 USD, but website shows 64.00 USD.
- **HG-021**: "Stainless Steel Kettle, 1.7 L" — Feed price is 48.00 USD, but website shows 44.00 USD.

To fix this manually, update the price in your product feed to match your product pages exactly and re-upload the data, as described in [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029).

Since automatic price updates are currently turned off in your settings, I also recommend turning on automatic item updates under the Automations tab in Merchant Center. This allows Google to automatically update small price differences using the structured data on your website to help prevent future disapprovals, as outlined in [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284).

Would you like to move on to the next issue?

turns.merchant: Why is my towel disapproved?
turns.reply:
You have no account issues and no warnings. 1 product is disapproved because its price in your product data does not match your website.

Here is the issue:

**Price mismatch (Disapproved)**
* **Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage** (ID: `HG-004`): Your product data listed the price as $32.00 USD, but your product page shows $36.00 USD.

**How to fix it:**
To fix this manually, update the price in your product data to match your website exactly ($36.00 USD) and re-upload it. Once updated, Google will recheck the page over the next few hours or days to approve it. Learn more in [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029).

Since your automatic price updates setting is currently turned off, you can also turn on automatic item updates under **Products > Automations** to help avoid price mismatches in the future. For more details, see [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284).

Would you like help with anything else?

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
